findings.title: T-15 cannot read a finding's run request, because its owner comes after it
quotes: Read the gap, where, right, run and tampering fields of a finding
Accepts: a finding's `run:` field, which must be a `TC-n` of `tests.md`; never command text
findings.fix: Move the `run:` field read (the `parse_lens` part of CT-12) into T-15 and add jury.py to its Files. Or make T-15 depend on T-16 and move T-15 after it. Either way, T-16 should not own a field that T-15 consumes.

sources.situation: T-15 must run a juror's requested TC and put its result in the next packs. The request is the `run:` field. T-15's Files are only `src/nio/evidence.py` and `tests/test_evidence.py`, and T-15 depends on T-5 and T-14 only. The worker has no parser for `run:`. The reader that would supply it is T-16, which depends on T-15. So TC-27 to TC-30 cannot be built from T-15 as written.

findings.reason: T-15 (depends on T-5, T-14) consumes a finding's `run:` field (CT-11 Accepts; TC-27 "a round-1 finding asks for a specific run"). The parsing of `run:` is bound to `parse_lens` (CT-12) and owned by T-16, which depends on T-15, so the order is inverted.
findings.note: T-15 now reads the run field itself and lists jury.py; T-16 no longer owns it

findings.title: T-28's acceptance test relies on a task it does not depend on
quotes: run through the QS-1 demo of T-29
findings.fix: Add T-29 to T-28's Depends on, or drop T-28's dependency on the demo and test the skill and ALLOW entry directly.

sources.situation: T-28 is marked parallel with T-29 and depends only on T-27. A worker that starts T-28 right after T-27 finishes has no QS-1 demo to run. Its Test line cannot be satisfied when the task is done.

findings.reason: T-28 depends only on T-27 and is parallel with T-29, but its Test line says "run through the QS-1 demo of T-29". The `--demo` runs exist only after T-29, which depends on T-20, T-24 and T-27, so T-28 can finish before the demo exists.
findings.note: T-28's test no longer runs through T-29's demo; TC-1 and its direct checks stand alone

findings.title: The test, lint and type-check commands have no mechanism, and the spec defers it
quotes: How a target project tells nio its test, lint and type-check commands (no mechanism today, RF-23)
findings.fix: Name the config keys and where they are read in one task (or in T-1 and T-5), or state the default when a key is missing. Then remove the DF-4 deferral, or the deferral and the contract cannot both hold.

sources.situation: T-5 must run the project's lint and type-check commands. No task says how the CLI learns which command to run, or which config keys to read (`tests.lint`, `tests.typecheck`, `tests.setup`, `jury.run_timeout`, `jury.max_runs`). The spec says that mechanism is deferred to #49. Two workers would invent different keys, and the fixture in tests.md sets keys that no task creates.

findings.reason: architecture.md lines 28-30 name `tests.lint`, `tests.typecheck` and `tests.setup` and say unset lint or typecheck is "not configured". CT-2 and CT-3 (contracts.md lines 27 and 41) give `jury.run_timeout` with default 600 and the same unset behaviour. DF-4 defers only the general mechanism for target projects, and `jury.max_runs` is in spec FR-16.

findings.title: "Known runner" is undefined, so skip and rerun detection cannot be built as written
quotes: the runner has no known way to run one test
a small passing test suite in `tests.suite`
findings.fix: List the supported runners and their skip and single-test syntax in the contract, or name the one runner the fixture uses and say unknown runners are reported as "couldn't run" for both checks.

sources.situation: T-7 must flag a newly skipped test (TC-12). Which skip syntax counts depends on the runner, and no artefact names any runner. The fixture in tests.md does not name one either. Given a pytest-style skip, one worker flags it and another, using a different runner, does not. The same gap affects T-15's rerun of a single named test (TC-27 to TC-30).

findings.reason: "Known runner" is the `RUNNERS` table in `src/nio/implement.py` (pytest, unittest, jest, vitest, mocha, go test, cargo test, rspec). architecture.md lines 59-62 and CT-11 Fails say a runner with no known single-test run gives "couldn't run".

findings.title: Secrets at the implementation gate has no owning code change
quotes: `IMPL_LENSES` in `jury.py`, the spec's trigger table row for row, used at this gate instead of `spec.LENSES`
Mode: direct: only tests are written, no code to lead
findings.fix: Name the secrets row of IMPL_LENSES as part of T-12's test list and Files, or state that IMPL_LENSES is read from the spec's trigger table at runtime and show that in T-12.

sources.situation: TC-48 needs the implementation plan to list security for `risk: [secrets]`. T-21 writes tests only. T-2 changes spec.py only, and T-12, which builds IMPL_LENSES in jury.py, does not list TC-48 or the secrets row. I infer that a worker who hard-codes IMPL_LENSES from the old trigger list omits secrets, so TC-48 fails and no task owns the fix.

findings.reason: The spec's trigger table (spec.md line 299) has a `secrets` → security row, and CT-8 makes `IMPL_LENSES` that table "row for row", so T-12 builds it with that row. T-2 adds the flag (CT-18), and T-21 proves TC-48 after depending on both T-2 and T-12, so ownership is covered.
